html:
SMTO-CTR-0003 — SMTO stopped writing the task plan because the task was stopped

GUID: 67e5e746-8474-43c1-bc93-02806b6c0727
Slug: task-contract-cancelled
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • The task was stopped while SMTO was still writing its plan (the Task Contract), so SMTO didn't act on this version of your request. Stopping doesn't undo anything done earlier.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you selected Stop on purpose, leave the task as it is. SMTO dropped the unfinished plan before acting on this version of your request, which is what Stop is for.
  2. Only if you still want the work done, start it yourself: select Continue task or Restart task if the task shows them, or send the request as a new message. SMTO never restarts stopped work on its own, so new work only begins when you choose it.
  3. If earlier tasks in this conversation made changes, check those changes yourself. Stopping this task does not reverse anything earlier tasks already did.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Stopped, and nothing new runs unless you start it.

If it still fails

  • If the task stopped although nobody selected Stop, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't assume the stop undid any earlier changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Task Contract compilation ended as cancelled because cancellation was observed before acceptance or the acceptance transaction found a pending Stop, so no revision was accepted.

What this means

  • Compilation observes cancellation before acceptance, or the acceptance transaction finds a Stop fence. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • Compilation observes cancellation before acceptance, or the acceptance transaction finds a Stop fence.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the task's cancellation/Stop state and current attempt identity.

How to fix it

  • No corrective action is required for this informational outcome.
  • Confirm the Stop or cancellation request on the run and the attempt's validation_state=cancelled in the Task contract activity. No action is needed if the Stop was intended; start further work only deliberately through Continue task, Restart task or a new request, and do not assume cancellation reversed effects of earlier revisions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Do not restart automatically. Inspect the retained outcome and start further work only when the user intends it.

How to verify the fix

  • Any deliberate new attempt occurs only after supported task controls permit it.

What not to do

  • Do not automatically restart cancelled work or assume cancellation reversed earlier effects.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
